title: A Study on Bias Detection and Classification in Natural Language Processing

bias_targets.methodology: Training and evaluating a DistilBERT-based classifier on aggregated datasets (including single-target sets like Hostile Sexism and multi-target sets) to detect and classify biased language targeting gender.
Evaluating a DistilBERT-based classifier's ability to detect race-targeted bias using aggregated multi-target text datasets (such as DynGen, MLMA, and StereoSet).
Using a DistilBERT-based classifier trained on datasets like CONAN and multi-target collections to detect and classify hate speech and bias directed at religious identities.
Evaluating a multi-target text classifier on aggregated dataset collections to identify biased language and stereotypes targeting specific professions.
Training and testing a transformer-based text classifier on multi-target datasets to detect biased language directed at people with disabilities.
Evaluating a DistilBERT-based text classifier on multi-target datasets to identify biased or hateful language targeting specific sexual orientations.
Evaluating a text classification model on multi-target datasets to detect biased language targeting gender identity (e.g., transgender and gender-minority individuals).
Using a text classifier trained on aggregated multi-target datasets to detect bias and hate speech directed at specific nationalities.

Attempting to evaluate a text classifier on multi-target datasets for age-directed bias, though the authors ultimately found the data too scarce (0.01% of entries) for effective measurement and dropped it in subsequent experiments.
